lead.hed: Coast Guard cutter Escanaba is home in Portsmouth after a Caribbean drug seizure
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted this afternoon from Portsmouth: the crew of Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba returned Monday after a 60-day patrol in the Windward Passage. On Aug. 29 the cutter, with a law-enforcement detachment embarked, stopped a vessel carrying about 2,082 pounds of marijuana, valued at more than $2.4 million. The crew later took aboard about 3,288 kilograms of cocaine transferred at sea from Cutter Richard Dixon and offloaded both loads in Port Everglades. Official still from the boat deck, Caribbean Sea, Aug. 20.
lead.image_credit: Petty Officer 2nd Class Nadia Sands · DVIDS 9963993 · Public domain · Escanaba deck crew on the boat deck before a small-boat launch, Caribbean Sea, Aug. 20, 2026.

political.hed: Theodore Roosevelt left San Diego on Sunday; Lincoln is near Hawaii
political.insight: USNI News, Monday: USS Theodore Roosevelt departed San Diego on Sunday with Carrier Strike Group 9, including Carrier Air Wing 11 and cruiser USS Chosin. The same fleet tracker puts USS Abraham Lincoln in the Pacific near Hawaii, homebound from Guam, and keeps USS George Washington and USS George H.W. Bush in the Arabian Sea. Positions as of Monday. No official still of Sunday's departure has been posted.

political.hed: Moscow's draft budget raises 2027 defense spending by about 27 percent
political.insight: Defense News, Monday, citing Reuters: government documents seen by Reuters put 2027 defense spending at 17.1 trillion roubles, about $202.6 billion, up from 13.5 trillion roubles originally budgeted. The papers also raise the 2026 deficit estimate to 3.2 percent of GDP from 1.6 percent. The government is expected to send the draft to parliament by Oct. 1. Draft figures, not a signed law.

political.hed: An essay asks what the ethics of government debt actually are
political.insight: Public Discourse, Monday: the essay says this is a good time to take the ethical questions around government debt seriously. Essay, not a budget vote. Not a ship story.

tech.hed: An airman shot down over Iran said the missing parachute was the terrifying part
tech.insight: Providence, Monday: an American weapons officer, callsign Dude 44 Bravo, ejected from a crippled F-15E over Iran and said looking up and seeing no parachute was the most terrifying thing he had seen. First-person account, not a new strike report.

culture.hed: A review says Thomas is on track to set the Court's longevity record
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Monday: Mark Pulliam reviews Sen. Ted Cruz's Going Further, a book drawn from interviews with Justice Clarence Thomas. The review says Thomas, with 34 years on the Court, is in second place behind William O. Douglas and would pass Douglas's record on May 19, 2028, if he stays. Book review, not a retirement announcement.

culture.hed: A philosophy professor says Augustine did not fuse Paul with Plotinus
culture.insight: American Reformer, Monday: Owen Anderson, who teaches philosophy at Arizona State, reads a footnote in Henry Chadwick's Confessions that treats Augustine as fusing Romans 1 with Plotinus. Anderson argues Paul teaches that creation reveals God, while Plotinus tells the soul to leave the material world behind. Essay, not a new translation.
